entries.title: How can a big drum be tuned to a note?
entries.answer: Timpani are bowl-shaped drums with skins or plastic heads stretched across their tops. Strike the drum with a soft-headed stick, and its stretched surface makes a clear note. Some timpani have a foot pedal that makes the head tighter or looser as the player moves it. Tightening the head raises the pitch. An orchestra often has several timpani so a player can use different notes in one piece.
facts: One of these drums is called a timpano, and several are called timpani.

entries.title: How did Duke Ellington write for his band?
entries.answer: Duke Ellington led a jazz orchestra and wrote music it could play. He knew the different voices of the people in his band, so a part for one player could sound different from a part for another on the same kind of instrument. Ellington also worked with other composers, including Billy Strayhorn. A band’s sound comes from what musicians write, how each performer plays, and how the players listen to one another.
facts: Billy Strayhorn wrote Take the “A” Train, which became a famous tune played by Ellington’s orchestra.

entries.title: How did Ella Fitzgerald use her voice like an instrument?
entries.answer: Ella Fitzgerald was a jazz singer known for the care she took with pitch and rhythm. At times she sang syllables without ordinary words, choosing sounds such as short pulses or long notes. This kind of singing is called scat. It can work like a trumpet or piano solo, where the performer makes musical choices as they go. Fitzgerald could sing familiar tunes in ways that made listeners hear new details.
facts: Ella Fitzgerald was known as the First Lady of Song.

entries.title: How do musicians know how loudly to play?
entries.answer: Dynamics tell musicians how loud or soft their music should sound. A group may begin so softly that you can barely hear it, then grow louder until the whole room seems full. That gradual increase is a crescendo. Written music often shows letters such as p for soft or f for loud. A player may make one short note stand out without making the entire song louder.
facts: Musical dynamics are different from tempo, which describes the speed of the beat.

entries.title: How do orchestra musicians play together?
entries.answer: An orchestra is a group of musicians who play different instruments together. A typical orchestra includes strings, woodwinds, brass, and percussion. The groups may play different parts at the same time. To line up their sounds, musicians follow written music and listen to each other. Many orchestras have a conductor who uses gestures to show when to start, how fast to play, or when to get quieter. The same group can make a tiny sound or fill a large room with music.
facts: Violins and cellos belong to the string family.
Trumpets belong to the brass family.

entries.title: How do written notes tell us what to play?
entries.answer: Written music gives performers a set of marks to follow. In a familiar kind of musical notation, notes sit on or between five lines called a staff. Moving a note higher on the staff usually shows that it should sound higher. The note’s shape can tell how long the player should hold it. A rest marks time when that player should be silent. People can learn and share many kinds of music by ear too. Written music is one way to keep a record that others can follow.
facts: A musical staff has five lines in common Western staff notation.
A rest can show a short silence or a long one.

entries.title: How does a flute make a sound without a reed?
entries.answer: A flute player blows a thin stream of air across an opening near one end. The air meets a sharp edge and sets the air inside the instrument moving back and forth. When the player opens or closes holes with keys, the air inside acts as if it has a different length. That helps change the note. A modern flute is commonly made of metal, but it belongs to the woodwind family.
facts: Most orchestra flutes are held sideways to play.

entries.title: How does a guitar change notes?
entries.answer: A guitar string makes a sound when you pluck it and it vibrates. On an acoustic guitar, those vibrations move into the body, which helps spread the sound. The small bars across the long neck are called frets. Press a string just behind a fret and the part that can vibrate gets shorter. Shortening the string raises the pitch, so two presses on the same string can make different notes.
facts: Guitar strings can also change pitch when a tuner changes how tight they are.

entries.title: How does a trumpet make different notes?
entries.answer: A trumpet player presses their lips to a small mouthpiece and blows so the lips buzz. The air inside the trumpet moves with the buzz. Press a valve and the air has to travel through an extra bend in the tubing. A longer route can help make a lower note. The player can also shape their lips and blowing to get different notes with the same valve positions.
facts: Most orchestra trumpets have three valves.

entries.title: How does a violin make a sound?
entries.answer: A violin player draws a bow across a string to make it vibrate. A small wooden bridge carries some of that motion into the body of the violin, which helps send sound into the room. The player can press a string down with a finger to shorten the part that vibrates. A shorter part usually makes a higher note. A violin can also sound when the player plucks a string.
facts: A regular violin has four strings.

entries.title: Is rhythm the same as the beat?
entries.answer: The beat is the steady pulse you can tap along to in much music. Rhythm is the pattern made by sounds and silences as time goes by. Try tapping slowly and evenly with one hand while a partner says “I can run.” Your partner can bunch the syllables together or stretch them across more than one tap. In an orchestra or a band, one person can play quick sounds while another plays slow ones, and both can still fit into the same beat.
facts: A pause can be part of a rhythm.
A rhythm can put several short sounds in the time of one beat.

entries.title: What did Mozart make with music?
entries.answer: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was a composer from Salzburg, in what is now Austria. He began making and playing music when he was very young and traveled with his family to perform. He later wrote for many combinations of musicians. An opera uses music to tell a story onstage, while a concerto gives a featured player a part to play with a larger group. Mozart wrote in both of these forms, as well as many others.
facts: Mozart wrote an early stage work called Apollo and Hyacinth as a child.

entries.title: What happens inside a piano when you press a key?
entries.answer: Press a key on an acoustic piano and it moves a small hammer hidden inside. The hammer strikes one or more strings tuned for that note and quickly pulls away. The strings vibrate, and a wooden soundboard helps spread the sound through the air. A padded part usually lands against the strings again when you let go of the key. A pedal can keep many of those pads raised so sounds last longer.
facts: An acoustic piano uses strings even though the player touches keys.

entries.title: What tells a musician how fast to play?
entries.answer: Tempo is the speed of the beat in music. Imagine walking with a steady drum tap. Fast taps make you take more steps in the same amount of time. Slow taps give you more time between steps. A musician may follow a printed word that says how fast to play, or a number that gives beats per minute. A piece can change tempo while it is being played, which can make it feel as if it is gathering speed or settling down.
facts: Sixty beats per minute gives one beat every second.

entries.title: What’s the difference between melody and harmony?
entries.answer: The melody is the line of notes you might hum when you remember a song. Harmony comes from notes sounding together or from the way groups of notes change underneath that tune. Imagine one student singing a tune while another holds lower notes that fit with it. You can still follow the tune, but the extra notes change how it feels. A piece can have more than one melody that fits together.
facts: A chord is a group of notes heard as a unit.

entries.title: Why do xylophones have bars of different sizes?
entries.answer: A xylophone has bars that ring out when a player taps them with mallets. The bars are often wooden, and differences in their lengths and shapes help give them different pitches. Some xylophones have tubes underneath the bars. The air inside the tubes can vibrate along with the bars, making the notes stronger. A player can make a tune by hitting several bars in order, just as a singer can sing several notes in order.
facts: Shorter bars often play higher notes than longer ones on the same instrument.

entries.title: Why does a cello sound lower than a violin?
entries.answer: A cello has long strings and a large wooden body. Its strings are tuned to make lower notes than the strings of a violin, and the body helps those sounds reach the air. A person usually plays a cello seated, with the instrument standing between their knees and an endpin resting on the floor. Like a violin player, they can bow or pluck the strings and press them to change the notes.
facts: The cello can play across a wide range of notes, including notes much higher than its lowest string.

entries.title: Why does a clarinet need a reed?
entries.answer: On a clarinet, a thin strip called a reed sits against a mouthpiece. When a player blows, the reed flexes quickly and sets the air in the tube vibrating. Fingers and keys open and close holes to help change the note. A player can also change how they blow to play notes in different parts of the instrument’s range. The same clarinet can sound quite soft or strong.
facts: A clarinet uses one reed at its mouthpiece.

entries.title: Why does a harp have so many strings?
entries.answer: A harp player plucks separate strings to make different notes. Short strings usually make higher sounds than long ones, and strings can also differ in thickness and tightness. A concert harp has foot pedals that can change how some strings are tuned, so the player can use more notes without adding another set of strings. Harpists can make several notes sound together or sweep a hand over many strings quickly.
facts: A concert harp usually has seven pedals, one for each letter name of the musical notes.

entries.title: Why does a trombone have a slide?
entries.answer: A trombone player starts a sound by buzzing their lips into the mouthpiece. The slide is made of tubes that can move into or out of other tubes. Push it outward and the air path grows longer, which can make the note lower. Move the slide smoothly while keeping the sound going and some notes can glide between pitches. Players also use their lips and breath to choose notes.
facts: Some trombones use valves, but the hand slide is typical in modern orchestras.

entries.title: Why does an oboe use two reeds?
entries.answer: An oboe player blows between two very thin pieces of cane. They are tied together near the base and can move quickly against one another at the tip. That movement helps create a vibration in the long tube. The player uses keys and fingers to cover or uncover holes to change notes. An oboe’s sound can stand out even when its part is fairly quiet.
facts: A double reed makes an oboe’s sound different from a clarinet’s single reed.

entries.title: Why is a double bass so big?
entries.answer: The double bass is the largest of the string instruments usually found in an orchestra. Its long, thick strings can move back and forth slowly enough to give it very low notes. In an orchestra, players can move a bow across the strings. In jazz and other kinds of music, they often pluck the strings with their fingers. The bass can help a group feel the beat and hear changes in harmony.
facts: A double bass player generally stands or sits on a high stool beside the instrument.

entries.title: Why is Louis Armstrong remembered in jazz?
entries.answer: Louis Armstrong grew up in New Orleans and became a celebrated jazz trumpeter and singer. He could take a tune listeners recognized and change the way some notes fell on the beat. Instead of playing only the same version each time, a jazz musician may invent part of the music while performing. Armstrong’s solos and recordings helped people hear what one featured player could do inside a band.
facts: One of Armstrong’s nicknames was Satchmo.
